  AUGUST 2023 MEETING MINUTES

A. Roll Call
a. A meeting was held at 7:08 pm in Community Room A located in the City Hall Lobby.
b. Commissioner Charles Braggs announced that he will step down from serving on the Parking and Traffic
  Commission. In addition, he added that his replacement will be Barbara Hibler as president of the Parking and
  Traffic Commission.
c. Charles Braggs served as District 1 Commissioner and Chairperson of the City of Inglewood Traffic and Parking
  Commission.
d. Commissioner Roberts and the committee are saddened by the news and wish him the best. In addition, the panel
  will miss the support that Commissioner Charles Braggs gave and provided.
e. Attendees included:
 Charles Braggs, Former Chairperson
 Barbara Hibler, Chairperson
 Richard Galindo, District 1
 Kip Rudd, District 2
 Brett C.S. Roberts, District 3
 Lois Hale, District 4
 Diana Maximo, Operations Manager (LAZ Parking)
 William Thompson, Traffic Operations Manager (LAZ Parking)
 Lieutenant David Salcedo, Police Department
 Peter Puglese, TE, PE, City Traffic Engineer
 Raquel Mendez, PTC Secretary

B. Approval of Minutes
a. June 2023 Meeting Minutes
 Commissioner Richard Galindo made a motion to accept the meeting notes. Seconded by Commissioner Kip
  Rudd. Three out of the five commissioners approved the minutes of the meeting. Chairperson Hibler and
  Commissioner Lois Hale abstained as they were not present.

C. Public Comments
 A resident of 117th and Crenshaw Blvd requested immediate attention for vehicle racing occurring at random
  hours of the night. Another issue the resident discussed was the installation of the residential parking permit sign.
  The resident asked for the installation date and reminded the commission that Mr. Thompson stated in October
  2022 that residential parking permit signs will be posted. The signs are not posted. Finally, the resident stated
  that it is not convenient for the City Council to change the sweep schedule and it would be better for the City
  Council to keep the sweeping schedule to the old schedule. Mr. Thompson stated that signs hours will be replaced
  with 7am to 1pm.

 A resident of 2nd Avenue and Century Blvd informed the commission of speeding vehicles including on the
  Century Blvd Local Access Road. The Police Department will review and investigate options to assist with the
  problem.

 A Second Avenue resident mentions that traffic on Crenshaw Boulevard becomes too heavy during the event.
  Driving to the stores is not feasible is one example. The resident also added that individuals are parking on the
  Home Depot locations preventing customer to find parking. Finally, the resident recommends that the City equip
  parking authorities with a better way of responding to the resident.

 A resident of Market Street in Council District 2 informed the Commission that Market Street between Hazel Street
  and Ivy Avenue is considered a residential permit parking district. It was also claimed that residents are fined for
  not having a parking permit or registration pass. When the resident inquired for information, the program does
  not allow the resident to register. The resident wants a response to avoid receiving a ticket.

D. Unfinished Business
a. None

E. New Business
a. None

F. Public Hearing
a. To amend the Citywide Parking Permit Program in District 9 at 2nd Avenue from 102nd Street to 104th Street
 On the date of the meeting, the following comments were given as to why the resident does or does not support
  the parking program:
   The program is inconvenient and unreasonable, not feasible to implement.
   The program must be aimed at visitors, not residents.
   Residents were unaware of the City's Parking Permit Program. The news was received when the resident
  saw the new parking permit sign being installed.
   The resident is aware of the need to have the Citywide Parking Permit Program, but not 24 hours a day, 7
  days a week program.
   Residents' preference is to have a sticker rather than use the license plate number.
   Giving too much information to the public is not something residents envision.
   The resident fears that another resident within the same block will report the resident's unregistered vehicle
   The program needs increased parking enforcement to be efficient and beneficial.
   Resident was in favor of the program due to the arrival of the new stadium in 2024.
   Resident was in favor of the program as traffic impacts the area and has seen unregistered parked vehicles.
  The problem observed is limited visitor parking and guests do not appear to be welcome.
 The Parking and Traffic Commission decided not to proceed with the voting process. The reason provided is
  more favorable to maintaining the program than to canceling it. Commissioner Roberts, made a motion to accept
  and was seconded by Commissioner Galido. All commissioners present voted to not proceed with the voting
  process to end the residential permit parking program.

G. Resolution
a. To terminate of the Citywide Parking Permit Program on 3rd Avenue from 90th Street to Manchester Boulevard
  within Distric 7B
 The resolution was signed by the Chairperson of the Parking and Traffic Commission. The resolution is attached
  to the minutes of this meeting for reference and documentation.
b. To terminate of the Citywide Parking Permit Program on 5th Avenue from 104th Street to 108th Street within
  District 9
 The City Traffic Engineer requested to abstain from presenting the resolution. Commissioner Roberts made a
  motion to accept and was seconded by Commissioner Galindo.

H. Referral from City Council/City Department
a. None

    PUBLIC RULES OF DECORUM
In compliance with the Ralph M. Brown Act and to further facilitate feedback, public comment is
encouraged at meetings of the City Council, its Authorities, Agencies, and Boards and Commissions, and
Committees and its Agencies, in accordance with the following rules. Please note Members of the
public are encouraged to contact the City Manager, or respective Operating Department Directors, first
before making service requests or service complaints directly to the Council.

    At the beginning of each meeting to consider Closed Session items, public comments are
  permitted to address one (1) or more Closed Session Items scheduled on the Agenda prior to the
  Inglewood City Council convening deliberations in private. Public comments during Closed
  Session shall not exceed a total of one (1) minute in length.

    At the beginning of each meeting to consider Open Session items (Consent Calendar, Warrants
  and Bills, Setting Public Hearings, Departmental Reports, Authority and Agency Items, Council
  Initiatives, etc.), public comments are permitted to address one (1) or more Open Session Items
  (excluding Closed Session Items, and Public Hearings) scheduled on the Agenda. Public
  Comments occurring at the beginning of Open Session shall not exceed a total of three (3)
  minutes in length.

    Public comments are not permitted on any scheduled Closed or Open Agenda item or Public
  Hearing in the event the item has been pulled from the Agenda, postponed or rescheduled for
  another date.

    Public comments to address a Public Hearing scheduled on the Agenda shall not to exceed 1
  minute in length.

    At the conclusion of the City Council meeting prior to adjournment, public comments are
  permitted on any items of interest to the public and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the
  City Council. Public comments occurring at the end of Open Session shall not to exceed one (1)
  minute in length.

    The Mayor, or Presiding Officer of the meeting may, at his or her discretion, restrict or grant
  additional speaker time based on such considerations as Agenda length, volume of speakers,
  complexity of item, or looming threat of loss of quorum.

    The Mayor, or Presiding Officer of the meeting may request that a spokesperson be chosen by
  the group to address the Council when a group of persons wish to comment on the same
  subject matter.

    Speakers are not permitted to cede their time, or any portion thereof, to another speaker.

    The Mayor, or Presiding Officer of the meeting, may invoke the use of speaker cards at any time
  use of such cards is deemed necessary to facilitate the orderly process of permitting public
  comment.
   All public comments are to be directed to the Mayor, or the Presiding Officer, and not to any
  other member of the public or to any single Council, Authority, Agency, Board, Commission, or
  Committee Member unless in response to a question from that Member.

  Any person making a public comment who wishes to provide written or other materials to the
  Mayor and Council must first request permission to approach the dais. If and when permission is
  granted, materials shall be given to the Sergeant At Arms for distribution.

  Commenters must be civil and respectful when addressing the Mayor and Council Members,
  and making reference to others.

  No person attending a public meeting shall engage in disorderly or boisterous
  conduct—including but not limited to applause, whistling, feet stamping, booing or making any
  loud, threatening, profane, abusive, personal, impertinent or slanderous uttering or comments.
  No person is allowed to disturb, disrupt, or otherwise impede the orderly conduct of the
  meeting.

  Members of the audience and speakers shall not wear or display signs, placards, banners, hats,
  costumes or similar items at any time in the Council Chamber that obstruct the view of the
  legislative body or audience members, or which creates sufficient disruption to impede the
  orderly conduct of the meeting or to intimidate other attendees of the meetings.

  Persons making public comment should not routinely expect to receive answers to questions
  posed during their remarks. Unlike Town Hall, Neighborhood Block, and other meetings and
  gatherings more conducive to question and answer format, City Council Meetings are business
  meetings. In many cases staff will be available to take speaker questions and contact
  information and respond in a timely manner.

  ENFORCEMENT OF RULES AND DECORUM
  The Mayor, or Presiding Officer of the Council or Committee, with the assistance of the
  Sergeant-at-Arms or any law enforcement officer, shall be responsible for maintaining the order
  of the meeting and uniformly enforcing the Rules of Decorum.

  In the event that any person breaches the Rules of Decorum, the Mayor, or Presiding Officer,
  shall order the person to cease the offending conduct.

  If any person continues to breach the Rules of Decorum in a manner that disturbs, disrupts or
  otherwise impedes the orderly conduct of the meeting following an order from the Mayor, or
  Presiding Officer, to cease the offending conduct, the Mayor, or Presiding Officer, may order
  that person to leave the meeting.

  If any person refuses to leave the public meeting following an order to do so from the Mayor or
  Presiding Officer, that person may be escorted out of the meeting by any law enforcement
  officer present and may be subject to arrest for violation of the California Penal Code or
  Inglewood Municipal Code.

DATE:  September 27, 2023

TO:  Parking and Traffic Commission

FROM:  Peter Puglese PE, TE, City Traffic Engineer

SUBJECT:  Request to Amend Residential Permit Parking District for 102nd Street between
  Century Blvd Local Access to 104th Street within District 9

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the Parking and Traffic Commission conduct a public hearing to do the following:
1. Receive Public Comments regarding the termination of Residential Permit Parking Program for 102nd
  Street between Century Blvd Local Access to 104th Street, within District 9; and
2. Provide direction to the City Engineer on how to proceed

BACKGROUND:
In June 2020, the City Council adopted a Citywide Residential Permit Parking Program. The program is
enforced 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with two-hour parking Monday through Sunday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
(Ordinance No. 20-09). The program was adopted to protect residential communities more effectively
and efficiently from non-resident vehicle intrusion.

On November 8, 2022, Public Works (PW) Department received a petition requesting the removal of
Residential Permit Parking on 102nd Street from 7th Avenue to 2nd Avenue. Due to the geometry of the
street and the addresses that sign the petition, the Department of Public Works recommends extending
the limits of petition for 102nd Street from Century Blvd Local Access to 104th Street. There is a count
of ninety-two (92) properties that are within the limit. Seventy-five (75) valid signatures (one signature
per residential unit) were submitted on the petition, resulting in eighty-two percent (82%) of all households
on the block signing the petition in favor of removing the permit parking restrictions. On September 8,
2023, a notice was sent to all addresses within the petition boundary to attend the September Traffic and
Parking Commission meeting to express their views on the matter.

DISCUSSION:
Residential Permit Parking Districts encourage residents to use their driveways to park their vehicles,
when available, so that those without driveways can park on the street. Public Works staff requests the
Parking and Traffic Commission provide instructions on how to proceed with the request by either:
1. Approve the request to start the voting process; or
2. Deny the request to end the processing of the petition.

A petition has been submitted to the Inglewood Public Works Department requesting the termination of
residential permit parking within District 9 on 102nd Street from 7th Avenue to 2nd Avenue. Due to the
geometry of the street and the addresses that sign the petition, the Department of Public Works
recommends extending the limits of petition for 102nd Street from Century Blvd Local Access to 104th
Street.

Per Sections 3-75 to 3-79 of the Inglewood Municipal Code, this matter will be presented to the
Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission at the time and place specified:

  Wednesday September 27, 2023 at 7:00 p.m.
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

This notice is being mailed to all addresses within the subject area. Any interested person may attend
this meeting and speak on this matter.

  Purpose of Public Hearing
The purpose of this public hearing is to give all residents of the subject area listed above an opportunity
to state their opinion of the subject matter.

The purpose of the Residential Permit Parking Program is to assure the availability to residents of some
on-street (curbside) parking spaces within a neighborhood where the patrons and/or employees of a
nearby commercial or industrial facility are otherwise using all available on-street parking spaces.

The Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission will therefore be considering if the availability of on-
street parking is severely impacted and if the termination of a residential permit parking within District
9 on 102nd Street between Century Blvd Local Access to 104th Street would be warranted. If it is
determined to be warranted, ballots will be mailed to each household within the subject area.

If a Residential Permit Parking District is terminated, all residents and visitors in this neighborhood will
not be restricted from parking on the public streets at any time; including during special events. If you
have any questions regarding this matter, or wish to express an opinion but are unable to attend the
public hearing, please contact the Inglewood Public Works Department at (310) 412-5333.

SUBJECT:  Request to Terminate Residential Permit Parking Program for 5th Avenue between
  104th Street and 108th Street

RECOMMENDATION:
It is requested that the Parking and Traffic Commission review the information included in this report and
approve the resolution to terminate the Residential Permit Parking Program within District 9 on 5th
Avenue between 104th Street and 108th Street.

BACKGROUND:
In June 2020, the City Council adopted a Residential Permit Parking Program. The program is enforced
24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with two-hour parking Monday through Sunday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
(Ordinance No. 20-09). The program was adopted to protect residential communities more effectively
and efficiently from non-resident vehicle intrusion.

On October 25, 2022, Public Works (PW) Department received a petition requesting the removal of
Residential Permit Parking for 5th Avenue between 104th Street and 108th Street. Fifteen (15) valid
signatures (one signature per residential unit) were submitted on the petition, resulting in forty-one
percent (41%) of all households on the block signing the petition in favor of removing the permit parking
restrictions.

On June 6, 2023, a notice was sent to the residents inviting them to the June Parking and Traffic
Commission meeting to express their views on the matter. The notice was sent to all residents within the
limits of the petition.

On June 28, 2023, the Parking and Traffic Commission held a public hearing on the issue of terminating
the Residential Permit Parking Program for 5th Avenue between 104th Street and 108th Street within
District 9. The Public Works Department requested that the Parking and Traffic Commission listen to
public comments and provide direction on whether the petition should go to a vote by the residents. As
a result, all district commissioners voted to approve the request to begin the voting process.

DISCUSSION:
On July 12, 2023, the Public Works Department mailed questionaries to each resident residing in the
boundary area of the petition and requested the questionnaires be returned within thirty (30) calendar
days. August 12, 2023 was the deadline for the City to accept responses to the questionnaires. On
August 15, 2023, the questionnaires were counted. Eleven (11) votes were cast to approve the
termination, while two (2) votes opposed the termination of the Residential Permit Parking Program. Five
additional ballots were received at the Department of Public Works office on August 17, 2023. Since
these ballots were received after thirty (30) days from the date of the ballot letter, they were not opened
or counted. Therefore, the vote count stands at eleven (11) votes to approve termination and two (2)
votes to oppose termination of the Residential Parking Permit Program.

Date:  Wednesday, July 12, 2023

To:  Residents of 5th Avenue

Subject:  Vote to Approve or Reject the termination of residential permit parking on
  5th Avenue from 104th Street to108th Street

The purpose of this letter is to allow residents the opportunity to vote on the removal of the
residential permit parking for 5th Avenue from 104th Street to 108th Street within District 9. By
voting "approve", this street will not be subject to the rules of a Residential Permit Parking
District. By voting "reject", this street will continue to have permitted parking and follow the
rules associated with it. The complete rules and procedures can be found in the Inglewood
Municipal Code Section 3-76 (Establishment of a Permit Parking District) through Section 3-
76.1 (Amending or Terminating a Permit Parking District).

Since the Parking and Traffic Commission has determined that permitted parking may not be
warranted in the area in question, ballots are mailed to all residences within the boundary of
the subject street.

If seventy-five percent (75%) or more of the returned ballots vote “approve” for the termination
of residential permit parking, then an ordinance amending the Residential Permit Parking
District will be submitted to the City Council for consideration. If approved, 5th Avenue from
104th Street to 108th Street within District 9 will not be subject to the Residential Permit
Parking District rules. Therefore, all vehicles can park on these streets without showing a
parking permit at all hours of the day, every day of the week. Additionally, the current parking
prohibitions for street sweeping will remain unchanged.

Using the enclosed ballot, please vote to approve or reject the termination of the residential
permit parking on 5th Avenue from 104th Street to 108th Street within District 9. Please return
the ballot to the City of Inglewood Public Works Department within thirty (30) days from the
date of this letter. Only one vote per household will be accepted. If you have any questions,
please do not hesitate to get in touch with the Public Works Department, at (310) 412-5333.

El propósito de esta carta es brindar a los residentes la oportunidad de votar sobre la
eliminación del permiso de estacionamiento residencial para la 3ra Avenida desde Manchester
Boulevard hasta la Calle 90 dentro del Distrito 7C. Al votar "aprobar", esta calle no estará sujeta
a las normas de un distrito de estacionamiento con permiso residencial. Al votar "rechazar",
esta calle seguirá teniendo estacionamiento permitido y seguirá las reglas asociadas con ella.
Las reglas y procedimientos completos se pueden encontrar en el Código Municipal de
Inglewood, Sección 3-76 (Establecimiento de un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso)
hasta la Sección 3-76.1 (Modificación o Terminación de un Distrito de Estacionamiento con
Permiso).

Dado que la Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico ha determinado que es posible que no se
justifique el estacionamiento permitido en el área en cuestión, las boletas se envían por correo
a todas las residencias en la calle descrita anteriormente.

Si el setenta y cinco por ciento (75%) o más de las boletas devueltas votan “aprueban” la
terminación del permiso de estacionamiento residencial, se presentará una ordenanza que
modifica el Distrito de estacionamiento con permiso residencial al Concejo Municipal para su
consideración. Si se aprueba, 3rd Avenue desde Manchester Boulevard hasta 90th Street
dentro del Distrito 7C no estará sujeta a las reglas del Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso
Residencial. Por lo tanto, todos los vehículos pueden estacionar en estas calles sin mostrar un
permiso de estacionamiento a todas horas del día, todos los días de la semana. Además, las
prohibiciones de estacionamiento actuales para el barrido de calles se mantendrán sin
cambios.

Usando la boleta adjunta, vote para aprobar o rechazar la terminación del permiso residencial
de estacionamiento en 3rd Avenue desde Manchester Boulevard hasta 90th Street dentro del
Distrito 7C. Devuelva la boleta al Departamento de Obras Públicas de la Ciudad de Inglewood

pregunta, no dude en comunicarse con el Departamento de Obras Públicas al (310) 412-5333.
